question: A shopkeeper lists the price of a fan at 50% above its cost price and offers a 10% discount on its list price. If he earns a profit of ₹56, then what is the list price (in ₹) of the fan?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

List Price (MP) = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150 units.

Selling Price (SP) = 150 − 10% of 150 = 135 units.

Profit = SP − CP = 135 − 100 = 35 units.

Given 35 units = ₹56 ⇒ 1 unit = 56 ÷ 35 = ₹1.6

List Price = 150 units × 1.6 = ₹240.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup percentage = 50%

Discount percentage = 10%

Profit earned = ₹56

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)
